reason: We already have an inverter in the house, and if it struggles with a washer I can buy a bigger battery for it, which also keeps the fans and lights running. Paying twenty-two thousand for a washer with its own battery that only does two cold loads feels like paying twice for the same thing, and nobody I know has one yet.
objection: Why should I pay for a second battery inside a washing machine when my inverter can do the job, and who has actually used this thing for two or three years to tell me the battery holds up?
would_change_my_mind: If my dealer or a relative in the village had been using one for a season and told me it saves them trouble that the inverter does not, and the price came down closer to an ordinary semi-automatic plus a little.
